title: Query count of the NAND continuation tree
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $B$ be a set of available coordinates among $n$ coordinates, let $a\in\{−1,1\}$, and let $T$ be a decision tree using coordinates in $B$. For any sign-valued input $x\in\{−1,1\}^{n}$, the NAND continuation tree makes zero queries if $a=1$, and otherwise makes exactly as many queries as $T$ does on $x$.
hypotheses_covered: set of available coordinates $B$ among the $n$ coordinates
